description: Two complete Overon synthesizer voices in one module, with a small mixer joining them into a stereo pair; each voice has two oscillators, a filter, two envelopes, an LFO and a VCA on their own jacks

params.text: Sets how loudly that voice appears in the stereo mix
Sets where that voice is placed across the stereo field
Spreads the two voices apart in both pitch and pan: at zero they are in unison and centred, and turning it up detunes them against each other and pushes them to opposite sides
Picks how incoming notes are shared out: Both plays every note on both voices, and Alt hands notes to the voices in turn so one note's release can overlap the next one's attack
Tunes VCO 1 of that voice coarsely, two octaves up and two octaves down from the pitch at its CV input
Sets how deeply VCO 1 of that voice is modulated: turned left the modulation moves its frequency, turned right its pulse width, and at the centre neither
Picks what modulates VCO 1 of that voice, ENV 1 or the LFO; a cable in the MOD SRC jack on its row overrides this switch
Sets the width of VCO 1's pulse wave on that voice, from a thin spike at one end to a full square at the other
Hard syncs VCO 2 to VCO 1 within that voice, restarting VCO 2's wave every time VCO 1's begins
Tunes VCO 2 of that voice coarsely, two octaves up and two octaves down from the pitch at its CV input
Sets how deeply VCO 2 of that voice is modulated: turned left the modulation moves its frequency, turned right its pulse width, and at the centre neither
Picks what modulates VCO 2 of that voice, ENV 2 or the LFO; a cable in the MOD SRC jack on its row overrides this switch
Sets the width of VCO 2's pulse wave on that voice, from a thin spike at one end to a full square at the other
Sets the cutoff of that voice's filter
Sets the resonance of that voice's filter, which self-oscillates at the top of its travel
Sets how deeply that voice's cutoff is modulated, one direction from the centre adding and the other subtracting
Sweeps the response of that voice's main filter output from lowpass, through notch, to highpass
Picks what modulates that voice's cutoff, ENV 2 or the LFO; a cable in the MOD SRC jack on its VCF row overrides this switch
Picks which of that voice's filter responses feeds its VCA, the LP / HP output or the bandpass
Crossfades VCO 1 into that voice's mix, its saw wave at one end and its pulse wave at the other, with the oscillator silent at the centre
Crossfades VCO 2 into that voice's mix, its saw wave at one end and its pulse wave at the other, with the oscillator silent at the centre
Crossfades between that voice's two external inputs; unpatched those are the internal noise and a 440Hz tuning tone
Turned on, that voice's cutoff follows the main CV, so its filter tracks the pitch of the notes
Sets how long that voice's ENV 1 takes to rise to full
Sets how long that voice's ENV 1 takes to fall from full to the sustain level
Sets the level that voice's ENV 1 holds while its gate stays high
Sets the speed of that voice's LFO
Picks what controls that voice's VCA: ENV 1, or the voltage at its VEL/EXT input
Sets how long that voice's ENV 2 takes to rise to full
Sets how long that voice's ENV 2 takes to fall from full to the sustain level
Sets the level that voice's ENV 2 holds while its gate stays high

inputs.text: The main pitch input, a volt per octave, shared out to the voices as the ASSIGN switch says
The main gate, shared out to the voices the same way
Velocity for both voices, or the direct VCA control where a voice's VCA switch is set to EXT; unpatched it reads as full
Sets the pitch of that voice's VCO 1, a volt per octave; unpatched it reads that voice's own CV input, and that in turn the main CV
Modulates that voice's VCO 1 in place of whatever the MOD SRC switch on its row picks
Sets the pitch of that voice's VCO 2, a volt per octave; unpatched it reads that voice's own CV input, and that in turn the main CV
Modulates that voice's VCO 2 in place of whatever the MOD SRC switch on its row picks
Moves that voice's filter cutoff, a volt per octave
Modulates that voice's cutoff in place of whatever the MOD SRC switch on its VCF row picks
An external signal into that voice's crossfade; unpatched it reads the internal noise generator
An external signal into that voice's crossfade; unpatched it reads a 440Hz tuning tone
A trigger here restarts that voice's LFO at the start of its cycle
Scales that voice's ENV 1, which is the usual way of applying velocity, or controls its VCA outright when that voice's VCA switch is set to EXT
The gate that runs that voice's ENV 1; unpatched it reads that voice's own gate input, and that in turn the main gate
The gate that runs that voice's ENV 2; unpatched it reads that voice's own gate input, and that in turn the main gate
That voice's own pitch input, a volt per octave, which takes priority over the main CV input
That voice's own gate input, which takes priority over the main gate input

outputs.text: Both voices summed, with the pan controls left out of it
Both voices mixed through their levels and pans, left side
Both voices mixed through their levels and pans, right side
That voice's VCO 1 sawtooth wave on its own, before its mixer
That voice's VCO 1 pulse wave on its own, before its mixer
That voice's VCO 2 sawtooth wave on its own, before its mixer
That voice's VCO 2 pulse wave on its own, before its mixer
That voice's main filter response, swept from lowpass through notch to highpass by its LP / HP knob
That voice's bandpass filter response, which its LP / HP knob does not affect
That voice's LFO on its own
That voice's audio output, after its mixer, filter and VCA, and before the stereo mixer
That voice's ENV 1 on its own
That voice's ENV 2 on its own

notes: patching a voice's own CV and GATE jacks turns this into two independent voices, since those take priority over the main inputs
every jack takes polyphony, and the voice count is the widest channel count across the main CV and gate jacks and each voice's oscillator, filter, envelope gate, CV and gate jacks
a monophonic cable in any jack is read by every polyphonic channel
menu: Randomize Voice 1 and Randomize Voice 2 — untick one to leave that voice alone when the randomize command runs, so a patch you like on one voice survives
Randomize Voice Controls — untick it to leave the two levels, the two pans, UNI/SPRD and ASSIGN alone when the randomize command runs
Copy Voice 1 -> Voice 2 and Copy Voice 2 -> Voice 1 — write every setting of one voice over the other
